zip_caveats: ZIPs do not tell you your ballot here. The City of San Diego splits into four congressional, three State Senate (plus one with no race) and six Assembly districts, and four council districts vote this year, so most ZIPs could hold more than one ballot. The Registrar's sample-ballot lookup (sdvote.com, under View Voter Information Pamphlet) shows your exact ballot; it asks for your house number, street, ZIP and birth date. City line: 92014 is only about 56% City of San Diego (the rest is the City of Del Mar), 92127 is about 60% city, and 92154 is about 95% city. 92118 is Coronado; only about 2,300 of its residents are in the City of San Diego, so it is not listed. Tiny slivers of 91911, 92025, 92027, 92067, 92071 and 92075 are in the city but are not listed. City Council: only Districts 2, 4, 6 and 8 vote this year, so voters in Districts 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 have no council race. District 2 runs from Clairemont to Point Loma; District 4 is southeastern San Diego; District 6 runs from University City to Scripps Ranch, including Mira Mesa; District 8 is the south, including Shelltown, Southcrest and San Ysidro. Council lines cut across ZIPs and we could not map them ZIP by ZIP. Supervisor: only District 4 (much of the city plus Lemon Grove and La Mesa) has a race that touches the city. Congress (Prop 50 map): about 534,000 city residents are in CD-50, 369,000 in CD-51, 322,000 in CD-52 (the border) and 165,000 in CD-49. CD-48 is in San Diego County but has no City of San Diego residents. State Senate: only even-numbered seats are up, so about half the city (SD-39, central San Diego) has no Senate race. SD-18 is all of 92136, 92154 and 92173 and parts of 92102, 92104, 92105 and 92113. SD-38 is all of 92014, 92092, 92093 and 92109 and parts of 92037, 92108, 92110, 92111, 92117, 92129 and 92130. SD-40 is all of 92121, 92122, 92126, 92127, 92128, 92131 and 92145 and parts of 92037, 92129 and 92130. Assembly: AD-78 (central) is all of 92103, 92108, 92111, 92116, 92117, 92119, 92120, 92123, 92124, 92126 and 92145; AD-77 (coast) is all of 92014, 92037, 92092, 92093, 92106, 92107, 92109, 92122 and 92140; AD-79 is all of 92105, 92114 and 92139; AD-80 is all of 92136, 92154 and 92173; AD-76 is all of 92127 and 92129; AD-75 is all of 92131. These ZIPs are split: 92101 (77/78), 92102 (78/79/80), 92104 (78/79), 92110 (77/78), 92113 (77/79/80), 92115 (78/79), 92121 (77/78), 92128 (75/76), 92129 (76/78) and 92130 (76/77). District numbers by ZIP come from 2020 census blocks and the 2021 maps. Schools: Measure M and the San Diego Unified board races are only for SDUSD voters, about three of every four city residents. About 136,000 city residents (92127, 92128, most of 92129) are in Poway Unified, about 67,000 (mostly 92130 and the city part of 92014) in the Del Mar Union, Solana Beach and San Dieguito Union High districts, and about 110,000 (92154 and 92173) in the Sweetwater Union High area. Those voters do not see Measure M and have their own school board races, which are not in this guide (Poway Unified, San Dieguito, Del Mar Union, Solana Beach, Sweetwater, San Ysidro, South Bay Union, Chula Vista Elementary, and the Palomar and Southwestern college boards). County Board of Education: Area 3 covers much of eastern San Diego inside San Diego Unified (all of 92105, 92115, 92119, 92120, 92124 and 92182 and parts of 92102, 92104, 92108, 92114, 92116 and 92131), and Area 5 covers the San Dieguito area (the city part of 92014 and most of 92130); other city voters have no Board of Education race (Registrar's precinct map). About 6,000 city residents in the Lemon Grove and La Mesa-Spring Valley school districts (parts of 92114 and 92115) may also see Grossmont-Cuyamaca college Measure G, La Mesa-Spring Valley Measure AA and Grossmont board races, which are not in this guide. The San Diego Community College District board races (Districts A and C) and water and other special-district races also follow their own lines. Use the lookup.

situations.short: Get a replacement or vote at any San Diego County vote center, including the Registrar's office.
situations.answer: San Diego County's deadline for a mailed replacement was 5 PM on October 27. Vote centers are open 8 AM to 5 PM through Nov 2, and 7 AM to 8 PM on Election Day; the Registrar's office at 5600 Overland Ave. is one too. You can vote at any San Diego County vote center.
